summary.name: OpenClaw Security Docs
summary.one_liner: A documentation hub covering OpenClaw's security trust model, audit tooling, and hardening guidance for running the Gateway.
use_cases: Auditing an OpenClaw install for configuration drift
Hardening a self-hosted AI agent gateway
Deciding whether to expose the Gateway beyond loopback
Restricting agent tool and messaging permissions
Responding to a suspected compromise of an agent deployment
summary.what_it_does: The page is an index of security documentation for OpenClaw. It states that regular host installs bind the Gateway to loopback, that most chat channels reply to unknown DM senders with a pairing code, and that group access is allowlisted behind a mention gate. It notes deliberate exceptions, such as container images defaulting to an exposed bind and some workspace channels trusting membership by default. It points to an audit command (openclaw security audit) that checks for drift from these defaults. Linked sub-pages cover the trust model, audit checks, hardened configuration baselines, access control, prompt injection, tool permissions, browser SSRF policy, network exposure, secrets handling, rate limits, and incident response.
notable: Built-in `openclaw security audit` command that checks for drift from safe defaults and can apply supported auto-fixes
Threat model mapped to MITRE ATLAS covering the OpenClaw platform and ClawHub
Copy/paste hardened baseline configs that keep the Gateway local, paired, and tool-restricted
Runbook for pre-flight and rollback checks before exposing the Gateway beyond loopback
caveats: Container images default to an exposed bind, so they must be paired with authentication
Some workspace channels such as ClickClack trust workspace membership by default
Agents with message-tool access can send across conversations and providers by default unless restricted
